correctness.rationale: The exact beta ODE follows from an integrable boundary-vanishing weighted derivative for all strictly positive endpoint exponents. Its integrated complex Wronskian has strict sign for nonzero asymmetry, so zeros on the real axis are impossible. Symmetric zeros are simple Bessel zeros. Parameter differentiation at any fixed simple symmetric zero gives the exact positive Bessel integral displacement, and standard fixed-order Bessel asymptotics give coefficient \(\tfrac12\log k+O(1)\). A separate numerical checker confirms representative identities and perturbed roots but is not used as an infinite proof.
